extracted.intended_audience: PR consultancies, national PR associations, PR professionals and communications leaders
extracted.subtask_description: High-level professional and ethical standards, skills expectations, and organisational practices promoted by ICCO for PR consultancies and national PR associations worldwide. The page describes values, member benefits, training, and priorities that imply criteria for professional PR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: To unite PR consultancies worldwide, raise professional standards, support learning, and provide a collective voice for the global communications industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO's mission statement frames raising professional standards as a core objective; membership gives access to international best-practice standards, research, and flagship events that support higher industry standards. Benefits referenced include access to thought leadership, advocacy, and participation in global initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with trust, ethics, collaboration, and long-term societal value
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a globally connected public relations profession that leads with trust, ethics, collaboration, and long-term value for society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as ICCO's vision and implies that PR work and organisations should prioritise trustworthy communications, ethical decision-making, collaborative behaviour, and communications that consider long-term societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and follow a common ethical framework; combat disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: The organisation emphasises a common ethical framework and proactive work to combat disinformation to strengthen trust in the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO highlights the value of a shared ethical framework and organised efforts against disinformation as ways to strengthen trust and reputation. Membership participation includes access to ethics frameworks and initiatives aimed at countering misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support continuous learning and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to education through webinars, courses, and the Global Diploma, supporting learning and skill development at every stage of a PR career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training & Professional Development is listed as a core service; ICCO encourages ongoing upskilling via courses, webinars and formal qualifications (Global Diploma), implying that competence should be demonstrable and continually refreshed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills expectation: be digital, analytical, and AI-fluent
rubrics_metrics.description: The skills base of the PR workforce is shifting fast — digital, analytical, and AI-fluent by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO's NextGen PR Report frames these capabilities as modern baseline expectations for practitioners, signalling that communications work should leverage digital tools, analytics, and AI competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data-led decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: Data-led decision making is becoming an entry-level expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes that decisions should be informed by data; this implies PR outputs (including campaigns and communications) should be planned, executed, and evaluated based on data and measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise purposeful work, flexibility and continuous learning (NextGen values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Younger communicators prioritise purposeful work, flexibility, and continuous learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO highlights these workforce priorities as criteria for organisational culture and the kinds of projects, roles, and learning opportunities that will attract and retain NextGen talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in global collaboration, knowledge exchange and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect PR consultancies and associations across countries, enabling collaboration, knowledge exchange, and a sense of belonging within a trusted international community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership and participation (e.g., board meetings, summits, regional meetings) are positioned as mechanisms to share best practices, showcase local achievements, and co-develop strategies — implying that high-quality PR practice involves active engagement with peers internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support diversity programmes and NextGen development
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in global initiatives such as ethics frameworks, diversity programmes, and NextGen development is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO lists these initiatives among membership opportunities, suggesting that organisations should commit to diversity and emerging-leader development as markers of good professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate and share impact through events, awards and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise and participate in global summits, forums, and awards that bring the industry together to share insight, recognise excellence, and discuss the future of communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICCO promotes events and awards as ways to surface best practice and raise standards, implying that demonstrable impact and peer-recognised excellence are part of the profession's quality criteria.
